title: celtis laevigata
intro: Celtis laevigata, commonly known as the Arizona hackberry, is a deciduous shrub or small tree native to the southwestern United States and northern Mexico. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its numerous health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which help to soothe digestive issues, reduce fever, and protect against oxidative stress. The therapeutic actions of Celtis laevigata include its ability to act as an anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant agent, making it effective in treating various health conditions. The bioactive constituents of Celtis laevigata include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and alkaloids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
